# September 27 MXFP8, MXFP4, and FP8 × MXFP4 collection

`kernels_best_0927.py` embeds the retained MXFP8 B2 and MXFP4 kernels plus
the tested five-stage FP8×MXFP4 alternative, with runnable launchers.
MXFP8/MXFP4 matrix-B-reuse optimizations are assembly overrides:

| Selector | Implementation | Saved tested assembly |
|---|---|---|
| `mxfp8_b2` | BK256, six-tile unroll + parent-B | `kernels_best_0927.amdgcn` |
| `mxfp4` | BK512, six-tile unroll | `kernels_best_0927_mxfp4.amdgcn` |

Both use delayed cluster wait, phase gap 1, 4×4 multicast, two data slots,
three scale slots, FP32 accumulation, and BF16 output. Both `trig` launchers
use hipBLASLt-equivalent data and block scales. MXFP4's shared generator is
`mxfp4_trig.py`; packed data and scales were validated byte-for-byte against
the C++ generator through full-size 4096×65536 operands.

## FP8 × MXFP4 five-stage alternative

Use **`--kernel fp8_mxfp4_five`** for the newly embedded five-stage kernel.
The original **`--kernel fp8_mxfp4`** still selects the September 17 nine-stage
implementation, which was faster in the comparison.

| Mixed-format kernel | Median us at 4096×4096×65536 |
|---|---:|
| September 13 | 228.940 |
| September 17 (default) | **228.670** |
| Five-stage alternative | 230.100 |

Four comparisons used the exact same random tensors and GPU allocations.
Five stages lost 4/4 against each baseline, taking 0.625% longer than
September 17. These are the completed experiment timings, not a new
packaging benchmark. The combined entry point is checked separately.

The alternative uses **three slots each for A, B, and B scales**. A is
unscaled FP8 and has no scale buffer. CTA tile: 256×256×256; 4×4 cluster
aggregate: 1024×1024×256. Six-tile unroll, phase gap 1, wait(4). Its schedule
is load low → compute both N halves → load high/arrive/advance → compute
both N halves → wait/refill tile t+3. Resources: 408 VGPR, 325816 bytes LDS,
zero scratch. No B-reuse override has been added to this mixed-format variant.

Mixed-format inputs retain their existing behavior: performance above used
random seed 42; its legacy trig mode uses indexed sin/cos and independent
random B scales, not the matched MXFP8/MXFP4 initializer.

Full-size validation of the combined CLI:

```bash
/usr/local/bin/gpu-lock bash experiments/fp8_mxfp4_five_stage_20260927/best_0927_check.sh
```

The underlying CLI command (run in the documented .rock/wpindex environment
under the GPU lock) is:

```bash
python3 third_party/amd/python/examples/gluon/gfx1250_gemm/kernels_best_0927.py \
  --kernel fp8_mxfp4_five -M 4096 -N 4096 -K 65536 \
  --input-mode random --seed 42 --check
```

See `experiments/fp8_mxfp4_five_stage_20260927/RESULTS.md` for the experiment
and `best_0927_check.log` in that directory for combined-source validation.
All three copied device functions are AST-identical to the standalone
`kernels_fp8_mxfp4_five_stage_0927.py`; the existing MXFP8/MXFP4 and mixed
baseline functions are preserved.

## Latest measured results

M=N=4096, K=65536. Each datatype has its own eight-pair benchmark round:

| Configuration | MXFP8 B2 us | MXFP4 us |
|---|---:|---:|
| Five stages + delayed wait + B reuse | **271.425** | **143.155** |
| Same source, no B reuse | 273.490 | 143.640 |
| Fresh hipBLASLt | 273.371 (solution 222) | 143.251 (solution 153) |

MXFP8 reuse won 8/8 pairs, saving 0.755%; its library reference was run at
10:55:00 UTC. MXFP4 reuse won 6/8 pairs, saving 0.338%; its library reference
was run at 12:18:51 UTC. The MXFP4 library difference is within observed
variation, so treat them as effectively tied.

These are the completed performance results before combining the sources.
Packaging did not initiate a new benchmark round.

## Five-stage schedule

| Stage | MXFP8 BK256 | MXFP4 BK512 |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Load low K128, both N halves | Load low K256 (two K128 chunks) |
| 1 | Compute low K128, both N halves | Compute low K256 |
| 2 | Load high operands/scales; arrive; advance | Load high operands/scales; arrive; advance |
| 3 | Compute high K128, both N halves | Compute high K256 |
| 4 | Wait; refill data t+2 and scales t+3 | Wait; refill data t+2 and scales t+3 |

Readiness uses `tdm.async_wait(4)` for MXFP8 and `tdm.async_wait(3)` for
MXFP4, whose A/B data and A/B scales use two fused copies per refill.
Leading stage 4 overlaps trailing stage 3 after the trailing group has
finished its LDS reads. Preserve slot lifetimes when changing the schedule.
Cluster arrive/wait are scheduling hints, not the multicast correctness
mechanism. MXFP4 retains its full accumulator and native [32,16,128] WMMA;
MXFP8 B2 uses split-N accumulators.

| Resources | MXFP8 | MXFP4 |
|---|---:|---:|
| VGPR | 479 | 496 |
| LDS bytes | 291192 | 303864 |
| Scratch bytes | 0 | 0 |
| Static WMMAs with B reuse | 576/768 | 528/704 |

## Run the complete configurations

From `/home/jungpark/mnt/gemm/triton`, use the scripts to compile the embedded
sources and rebuild their B-reuse overrides for the requested shape:

```bash
# MXFP8: correctness, paired benchmark, fresh hipBLASLt last
/usr/local/bin/gpu-lock bash experiments/mxfp8_b2_edges_20260926/best_0927.sh

# MXFP4: full-size correctness, eight pairs, fresh hipBLASLt last
/usr/local/bin/gpu-lock bash experiments/mxfp4_five_stage_20260927/best_0927.sh

# MXFP4: only validate the combined entry point
/usr/local/bin/gpu-lock bash experiments/mxfp4_five_stage_20260927/best_0927.sh --check-only
```

Scripts select `.rock` / `/home/jungpark/mnt/wpindex/triton` and clear
conflicting compiler/profiler environment settings. They generate overrides
from each compile instead of blindly using saved full-size assembly on other
shapes. The assembly transformations only add eligible B-reuse modifiers.

Plain Python CLI execution runs **without B reuse**. Select:
- MXFP8: `--kernel mxfp8_b2 --mxfp8-b2-experiment unroll6-parent`.
- MXFP4: `--kernel mxfp4`.

The dated source embeds both implementations. It does not import the
standalone five-stage MXFP4 kernel or experiment modules. Package exports
and older source snapshots remain available; other kernel selectors are
inherited experiments rather than newly promoted kernels.

## Provenance and validation

MXFP8 functions remain unchanged from the original best_0927 snapshot.
The two new MXFP4 functions are AST-identical to
`kernels_mxfp4_five_stage_0927.py`; existing helper functions are preserved.
The MXFP4 launcher now selects the embedded five-stage implementation and
the validated input generator. Saved assembly files are byte-identical to
the tested overrides. Hashes are recorded in
`experiments/mxfp8_b2_edges_20260926/best_0927_manifest.json`.

Original MXFP8 correctness: K1024 trig, K1536 random, K65536 trig.
Original MXFP4 correctness: K2048 trig, K7168 random (unroll/remainder),
K65536 trig, with and without reuse. Combined-source full-size correctness passed with and without B reuse;
resources remain 496 VGPR and zero scratch. Validation is recorded in `experiments/mxfp4_five_stage_20260927/best_0927/check65536.log`.
